To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HHT patients have a genetic mutation that affects the TGF-β/BMP pathway and leads to vascular abnormalities.
HHT patients have an altered balance of pro- and anti-angiogenic signaling pathways in endothelial cells that leads to vessel destabilization and vascular abnormalities.
HHT is caused by a defect in TGF-β/BMP signaling in endothelial cells, which results in a loss of pericyte coverage and vessel destabilization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms of vascular abnormalities in HHT.
the development of a new therapeutic strategy to treat HHT by promoting the stability of the blood vessel wall and reducing vascular malformation development.
the role of TGF-β signaling and pericyte coverage in the development of HHT and the potential of TGF- β and VEGF inhibitors to treat this disorder.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

vessel normalization is a promising approach to treat HHT and that the concept of vessel destabilization in the pathogenesis of HHT can be used as a basis for the development of novel therapies for HHT.
the vascular malformative process in HHT is caused by a loss of perivascular support cells and a subsequent loss of vessel stabilization.
the endothelial cell is not the only cell type responsible for the vascular abnormalities observed in HHT, but that pericytes and other mural cells also play a role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the loss of pericytes and the subsequent loss of pericyte coverage of blood vessels in HHT is a result of decreased TGF-β signaling activity and increased VEGF signaling activity in the endothelium, and that normalization of these signaling activities can restore the blood vessels to a more stable and functional state in HHT.
the TGF-β/BMP and the VEGF signaling pathways are critical for the maintenance of blood vessel stability and the prevention of HHT vascular malformations.
the loss of pericytes is a major contributor to HHT development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HHT represents an ideal disease model to test novel therapies aimed at stabilizing the vascular system.
the endothelium is not the only player in HHT development and that the pericytes, which are the mural cells of the blood vessels, play a key role in the pathogenesis of this disease.
vessel normalization can be a promising therapeutic strategy for HHT.
